item.title: New Observations Show How Black Holes Stir Up Material Surrounding A Galaxy
item.description: Supermassive black holes power tremendous jets that extend far beyond their galaxy. A new study finds how they can also warm material at the outer edge of a galaxy and reduce the rate of star production over time.

item.title: A Distant Supercluster of Galaxies Points To Self-Interacting Dark Matter
item.description: The El Gordo supercluster is unusually large given its distance. How could such a large galaxy cluster form so quickly? The answer could be that dark matter is self-interacting in an interesting two-state way.

item.title: The telescope that could reveal what dark matter and dark energy are
item.description: The Roman telescope is NASA’s newest space observatory. Every 10 months, it will get the equivalent of about 1000 years' worth of Hubble observations. Will it find the answers to our questions about dark matter and dark energy?

item.title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.27059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. item.title: Webb Captures This Golden Galaxy Cluster in All it's Glory
item.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features the brilliant golden galaxies belonging to the MACS J0454.1-0300 galaxy cluster.

item.title: Graph Neural Networks for Astrophysics and Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2610.27051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics seldom makes breakthroughs when we consider objects only in isolation. item.title: Slow-Roll Inflation at Arbitrary Order
item.description: arXiv:2610.28608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive explicit expressions for the primordial scalar and tensor spectra at arbitrary finite order $p$ in the slow-roll expansion, valid both for canonical single-field inflation and $k$-inflation. item.title: Leviathan: a very massive, extended sub-millimetre galaxy spectroscopically confirmed at rm z = 4.05
item.description: arXiv:2610.27101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Leviathan, a sub-millimetre galaxy (SMG) spectroscopically confirmed at $z=4.051$ with JWST/NIRSpec. Modelling 31 bands of photometry from the rest-frame ultraviolet to the millimetre, we find a stellar mass of $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=11.34^{+0.15}_{-0.22}$, making Leviathan one of the most massive spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at $z>4$, yet consistent with $\Lambda$CDM for a star-formation efficiency of approximately 20%.
